nodes.description: Mice with one inactivated Gnal allele. They have half the normal striatal G-alpha-olf, no overt dystonia at baseline and mild motor and behavioural changes, and develop dystonic postures and movements after systemic or intrastriatal oxotremorine. The authors propose untreated and treated mice as models of presymptomatic and symptomatic disease.

CRISPR-generated rats heterozygous for a frameshift in the Gnal isoform that predominates in human and rat striatum. They show early reduced locomotion, poor rotarod performance and impaired motor learning, loss of corticostriatal long-term depression rescued by A2A receptor blockade, and reduced adenylyl cyclase 5 and D2 receptor levels.

Germline GNAL variants, most often missense and spread across the helical and Ras-like GTPase domains, with a minority of nonsense, frameshift, start-loss and splice variants. Truncating variants and several missense variants abolish or reduce activation of G-alpha-olf by the D1 receptor in bioluminescence resonance energy transfer assays, so loss of function is the accepted effect. One review found loss-of-function variants associated with faster generalization than missense variants, a result its authors call hypothesis-generating. The GNAL gene binding sits on the next node, with the molecular function it encodes.

nodes.description: Virtually all striatal projection neurons contain G-alpha-olf and no detectable G-alpha-s, so G-alpha-olf is required for adenylyl cyclase responses to dopamine through D1 receptors in direct-pathway neurons and to adenosine through A2A receptors in indirect-pathway neurons. In mice with one inactivated Gnal allele, striatal G-alpha-olf is halved and receptor-stimulated cAMP production is reduced; heterozygous rats also show reduced adenylyl cyclase 5 and secondary changes in A2A and D2 receptor levels. Basal cAMP is unchanged. Cell-type-specific deletion confirms that G-alpha-olf is needed for D1 and A2A receptor coupling in the respective neuron types.

nodes.description: G-alpha-olf is the stimulatory G protein alpha subunit that, with beta-2 and gamma-7 subunits, transduces dopamine D1 and adenosine A2A receptor signals to adenylyl cyclase 5 in the striatum, and odorant receptor signals in olfactory neurons. Its level is rate-limiting for D1 receptor activation of adenylyl cyclase 5, so halving it reduces signalling. Disease variants either fail to support any D1 receptor response or impair association with G-beta-gamma and the amplitude of the response.

nodes.description: The striatal circuit level at which the cellular defects are thought to produce dystonia. Gnal heterozygous mice show only mild motor and behavioural changes at baseline, with altered striatal spine morphology, but develop dystonic postures and movements after a cholinergic agonist given systemically or into the striatum, not into the cerebellum. Heterozygous rats have reduced locomotion and impaired rotarod performance and motor learning. Increased cerebello-thalamic excitability has also been recorded in the mouse model; whether the cerebellum contributes independently is recorded as an open question.
